problem_summary.summary: Determine whether every node obeys the strict BST ordering rule across its entire subtree, not only against its parent.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: the root of a binary tree. Return true exactly when every left-subtree value is smaller and every right-subtree value is larger at each node.

brute_force.explanation: Collect all values with iterative inorder traversal, then check that every value is strictly greater than its predecessor.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A binary tree is a valid BST exactly when its inorder sequence is strictly increasing. The list check rejects duplicate values and any ancestor-bound violation because either would break that ordering.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — the traversal and strictly increasing check each take linear time.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for all inorder values and the traversal stack.

optimized.explanation: Traverse iteratively with a stack of frames carrying the exclusive lower and upper bounds allowed for each node. Reject a value outside its inherited bounds.
optimized.correctness_idea: A node's value must be greater than every ancestor bound on its left and less than every ancestor bound on its right. Each child frame tightens the appropriate bound, so a node passes exactly when it satisfies all ancestor constraints. Exclusive comparisons also reject duplicates.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is checked once and each edge creates at most one frame.
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary for the explicit depth-first stack, where h is tree height.

steps.event: Check root value 8 with the initial range.
steps.condition: 8 is strictly inside the initial bounds.
steps.action: Accept 8 and push right and left child frames with bounds based on 8.

steps.condition: 4 is strictly inside its inherited range.
steps.action: Accept 4; it has no children, so continue with the pending right subtree.

steps.event: Check node value 12 and enqueue its children.
steps.condition: 12 is valid, and its left child must remain greater than 8.
steps.action: Push 14 with range (12, +infinity), then 6 with range (8, 12).

steps.event: Check node value 6 in the right subtree of 8.
steps.condition: 6 <= lower bound 8, even though it is greater than its parent 4 would be.
steps.action: Reject because this node violates an ancestor's strict lower bound.

edge_cases.case: A child value violates a distant ancestor bound
edge_cases.handling: Inherited lower and upper bounds catch violations that a parent-only comparison would miss.
Strictly increasing inorder values and exclusive bounds both reject duplicates.

edge_cases.case: Node value is Integer.MIN_VALUE or Integer.MAX_VALUE
edge_cases.handling: The optimized method uses long bounds beyond the full int range instead of int sentinels.
Both implementations use explicit stacks and avoid recursive stack depth.
